SKAN Group AG (SKAN-CH): a high-quality niche leader whose recovery is real and already in the share price, with the upside skew in margin and cash, testable on 28 January and 23 March 2027

Investment memo, 26 November 2026. For Richard. Money in CHF millions unless stated; per-share figures in CHF. Definitions and sources are in the end notes.

#0 Summary of key insights, implications and conclusions

The verdict: a fair set-up today, with a clear route to a positively skewed one by 23 March 2027

  • What is priced: SKAN's volume recovery. The share price rose 48% in twelve months while the sell-side's 2027 EPS fell 30%.
  • What is not priced: a cost base that has stopped growing, and the cash that the end of heavy investment releases. Both report first, on 28 January and 23 March 2027.
  • What to watch: second-half 2026 orders above about CHF 220m, a second-half EBITDA margin of 19% or more with headcount at or below about 1,700, and a 2027 guide that a flat cost base can visibly beat.

The case in one paragraph. SKAN is the world leader in isolators, the sealed enclosures in which sterile and toxic injectable drugs are filled. Regulation is pushing the drug industry onto SKAN's product, SKAN's own order cycle troughed in the first half of 2025, and SKAN now holds a record order book. The share price has already paid for that recovery in volume, so the next leg of the share price has to come from earnings. The part of the earnings story that the market has not yet put into its numbers, a cost base that has stopped growing, is also the part that reports first.

The eight conclusions that matter

  1. Trust the earnings destination more than its date. About CHF 70m of EBITDA on about CHF 435m of sales (model EPS of about 1.80) asks nothing of SKAN that SKAN has not done before: it is 2024's equipment year repeated on a larger service base. I hold that earnings level with high confidence, but its arrival in calendar 2027 with only moderate confidence, because customers decide when their projects are delivered.
  2. The positive skew is in margin and cash. SKAN's fixed costs have been flat for five half-years while half-year sales swung by half, headcount is falling, and capital spending is roughly halving as a share of sales. Yet the sell-side's 2027 EBITDA margin is still below 2024's margin on a quarter more sales.
  3. The negative skew is in revenue timing and in the 2028 to 2029 estimates. One customer can push one project a year later, and nothing can pull a project a year earlier. The sell-side's outer-year estimates carry SKAN's mid-term target forward at 15% to 20% annual growth, where the model has 9% to 11%.
  4. The order of events favours the holder for two more reporting dates. The under-discounted positives (margin, cash and a beatable first 2027 guide) show on 28 January, 23 March and in August 2027. The under-discounted negatives (the order rate after 2027, share loss to turnkey line builders and a slower ramp of the new PAS business) show from late 2027.
  5. The sell-side's estimates are wrongly composed rather than too low. For 2026 and 2027 the model's EBITDA equals the FactSet figure, but on lower sales and a higher margin. Near-term revisions to EPS should therefore net to about nil. The first real chance of an upgrade to a current-year estimate is the August 2027 half-year report.
  6. The headline valuation gap depends on whose earnings are used. The share is 22% below the guideline fair multiple on the sell-side's EPS, 10% below on model EPS and about 5% or less below on attributable EPS.
  7. The 18-month return leans on a re-rating; the three-year return does not. The model shows a total return of +23.5% to end-2027 and +47.3% to mid-2029 at the guideline multiple of 34.8x. Over three years, earnings growth alone would absorb a fall to the tenth-percentile multiple.
  8. Three readings would turn a fair set-up into a positively skewed one. They are second-half 2026 order intake above about CHF 220m, a second-half EBITDA margin of 19% or more with year-end headcount at or below about 1,700, and a first 2027 guide that sits visibly below what a flat cost base can deliver. All three readings are known by 23 March 2027.

The five judgements that move the shares, with the arithmetic

Five judgements in the model carry most of the value; delivery timing (J1) is the largest single risk to EPS, and cost discipline (J2) and order intake (J3) carry the largest upside. The arithmetic is mine, on the model's 2027 and 2028 figures, with tax at 17%, 22.5m shares, materials at about a quarter of sales, and all other costs fixed within a year.

  • J1: a slipped equipment project costs about three times its share of sales in EPS. CHF 10m of sales moving out of a year removes only about CHF 2.5m to 3m of materials cost, so EBITDA falls by CHF 6.5m to 7m. After tax that is CHF 5.4m to 5.8m, or 0.24 to 0.26 a share: about 14% of 2027 EPS for 2.3% of sales. A project of CHF 30m to 40m whose manufacturing phase slips takes CHF 15m to 30m of sales with it, and so CHF 10m to 20m of EBITDA and 0.37 to 0.74 of EPS. The revenue is deferred, not lost: 2028 gains roughly what 2027 loses.
  • J2: each 1% of cost growth saved adds about 0.09 to 2027 EPS. Non-material costs are about CHF 234m in 2026 (sales of 387.0 times 0.75, less EBITDA of 56.1). Each 1% of that cost base is CHF 2.3m of EBITDA, half a point of 2027 margin and 0.09 of EPS. The model's 2027 EBITDA of 69.8 implies that the cost base grows by about CHF 19m to 23m. At 7% cost growth EBITDA is about 76.6 (17.6% margin); at 5% it is about 81.3 (18.6%); at 12% it is about 64.9 (14.9%). The offset to watch is the material ratio: one point of the material ratio on 2027 sales is CHF 4.4m, the same as two points of cost growth. Within J2, each point of S&C margin is CHF 1.7m of EBITDA and 0.06 of EPS.
  • J3: extra 2028 sales are worth far more if SKAN delivers them without hiring. An extra CHF 24m of 2028 sales drops through to EBITDA at 65% to 70% if the cost base is unchanged (CHF 16m of EBITDA, 0.59 of EPS), but at only about 25% if SKAN hires to deliver it (CHF 6m, 0.22). Equipment sales flat at 267 instead of 288 remove CHF 21m of sales, CHF 14m to 15m of EBITDA and about 0.53 of EPS. Each 0.10 of two-year-forward EPS is worth CHF 3.5 a share at 34.8x, or 5% of the price.
  • J4: PAS matters for 2028 and 2029, not 2027. CHF 10m of PAS sales is worth about CHF 5m of EBITDA and 0.18 of EPS. A further year's slip in PAS takes 2028 PAS sales from 14 to 5 and 2029 PAS sales from 24 to 14: CHF 4.5m to 5m of EBITDA and 0.17 to 0.18 of EPS in each year. PAS sales of 36 in 2029 instead of 24 add CHF 6m of EBITDA and 0.22 of EPS.
  • J5: each turn of multiple is worth 3.5% of the share price. The model capitalises two-year-forward EPS of about 2.41 at end-2027, so each turn of multiple is CHF 2.4 a share. Topic #12 gives the full table.

#1 Tailwinds in the operating environment, and the headwinds

The operating environment gives SKAN volume but withholds price: the tailwinds dominate through 2027, and the headwinds act on orders from 2027.

>90%of new filling lines now specify isolators, against 40% to 50% historically
442.3record backlog: 1.22x trailing sales, against 0.88x at end-2024
+49%Americas order intake in H1 2026, now about 40% of the group
~70% → ~50%SKAN's share of process isolators over two years, by a competitor's estimate

Evidence: three forces push demand into SKAN's product at the same time, and SKAN's own cycle has turned.

  • Regulation. The EU's Good Manufacturing Practice rules for sterile medicines (Annex 1, in force since August 2023) and the US Food and Drug Administration's contamination-control expectations favour sealed isolators over open cleanrooms. Over 90% of new filling lines now specify isolators (an Optima sales manager, 29-Jul-25; a competitor), and about 1,200 legacy fill-finish suites face upgrades.
  • Drug mix. Antibody-drug conjugates and other toxic injectable drugs cannot be sterilised after filling, so they need aseptic-toxic filling lines, which are SKAN's highest-value niche. Several orders in the double-digit millions for such lines arrived in H1 2026.
  • Onshoring. Lonza estimates that only about 5% of the roughly USD 600bn of announced US drug-manufacturing investment has broken ground, so most of the US order flow is still to come.
  • SKAN's own cycle. Order intake rose 16.3% to 247.6 in H1 2026.

Evidence: four headwinds act on SKAN's market share, its prices and its order rate after 2027.

  • Turnkey rebundling. Filling-machine makers (Syntegon, Optima, Bausch+Ströbel, IMA) increasingly sell the whole filling line with their own isolator. Management disputes the competitor's share estimate: it reports a stable 30% to 40% share of all isolators and says SKAN won most of the larger US fill-finish projects in H1 2026. Both accounts can be true if SKAN is ceding standard lines while holding complex ones.
  • Buyers. The fastest-growing customer groups, contract manufacturers and biosimilar makers, are the most price-conscious.
  • The customers' capital-spending cycle. Deutsche Bank expects large-pharma capital spending to peak in 2027 and fall 1.3% in 2028. Contract manufacturers have spare capacity. Demand for GLP-1 (weight-loss and diabetes) injectables is moderating, as Stevanato's reset of 3-Nov-26 showed, and GLP-1 projects were about 15% of SKAN's 2024 orders.
  • The Swiss franc. Most SKAN projects are priced in francs and hedged from signature, so a stronger franc arrives over one to three years as lost competitiveness against euro-priced rivals in tenders. A sustained 10% rise in the franc is worth perhaps 4% to 8% of EBITDA over two years.

InferenceRegulation works as a ratchet, because sterility rules do not loosen, so the volume tailwind is durable. The headwinds do not touch the backlog already in hand; they act on what customers order from 2027. Through 2027 the tailwinds therefore dominate. For 2028 and 2029 the outcome is a race between US onshoring orders arriving (expected mainly in H2 2027, with revenue in 2028) and customers' capital budgets flattening.

So what. SKAN's revenue to 2027 is about as well supported as revenue in a project business can be, but nothing outside the company will lift its margin. The model therefore holds real equipment prices flat and slows equipment sales growth to 8% in 2028 and 5% in 2029.

Against the marketI agree with the market on the drivers and on 2026 to 2027, which the share price reflects. I differ on 2028 to 2029. The sector's debate about a capital-spending plateau and turnkey buying has not been applied to SKAN, because the analysts who follow that debate do not cover SKAN. One detail shows the blind spot: Deutsche Bank's survey of injectable-drug specialists (13-Nov-26) names Syntegon, Bausch+Ströbel and Optima as preferred fill-finish vendors, and SKAN is absent because the survey asked about the whole line, not the isolator.

Strongest counter-caseSKAN may not face a plateau at all. Annex 1 upgrades and cancer-drug lines do not wait for US mega-plants, Repligen's equipment orders were at a five-year high in Q3 2026, and onshoring orders would land on top in H2 2027. On that reading 2028 sales growth is in the mid-teens and UBS's 2028 sales of 508 are right (J3).

What would change my viewSecond-half 2026 order intake, reported on 28 January 2027. A strong figure with US projects in it would move me toward the no-plateau case; a weak figure would say the headwinds have arrived early (the thresholds are in topic #9). A filling-machine partner dropping SKAN from joint bids would matter more than either.

Conclusion: the tailwinds are strong, durable and already visible in a record order book, but they deliver volume without price, and three real headwinds begin to bite on orders from 2027.

Score: 70, set by the Rater. Enacted regulation (Annex 1, over 90% of new lines now specifying isolators, about 1,200 legacy suites to upgrade), ADC demand and US onshoring reach most of sales and already show in a record backlog of 1.22x sales, so revenue to 2027 is well supported; but the forces bring volume without equipment price, and direct threats (turnkey line builders taking standard-line share, a large-pharma capex plateau in 2028, GLP-1 moderation, the franc) act on orders from 2027. I sit above the External group's 65 because the regulatory ratchet is written into rules and order books, and just below Eckert & Ziegler's structural, barrier-protected tailwind because of the share and price leakage.

#2 Internally-driven corporate change forces, and the problems

SKAN has moved from building capacity to harvesting it: its cost base has stopped growing, and the sell-side's numbers do not yet reflect that change.

17% to 23%of each extra franc of sales kept as EBITDA in the growth years 2023 and 2024
48%of each extra franc of sales kept as EBITDA in H1 2026
15.4% vs 15.8%sell-side 2027 EBITDA margin, against 2024's actual margin, on 26% more sales

Evidence: four changes point to harvesting.

  • Costs have stopped growing. Operating costs other than materials were 104 to 107 in every one of the five half-years to H1 2026, excluding the businesses acquired in August 2025, while half-year sales ranged from 135 to 199. Headcount fell by 61 to 1,694 in H1 2026, through what management calls "targeted measures" whose full-year effect comes in 2027. Other operating expenses fell 9.5%.
  • A new operator. Jonas Greutert became chief executive on 1 January 2026 after five years on Mettler-Toledo's executive board. He has introduced profit accountability by segment, confirmed rather than raised guidance while orders rose strongly, and kept a backlog item of CHF 15m to 20m that is at risk of cancellation in plain view and outside the plan. SKAN has also scheduled a preliminary release for 28 January 2027, a date that was not in its calendar in 2024 or 2025.
  • The investment phase is ending. Capital spending was 53.8 in 2024 and 45.9 in 2025, about 14% to 15% of sales. The model has 30 to 38 a year, about 7% to 8% of sales. The chief financial officer spoke on 24-Mar-26 of "mid-single-digit levels" for 2026 and 2027. If he meant per cent of sales, capital spending would be about CHF 20m to 24m, and free cash flow would be CHF 8m to 12m a year above the model.
  • Mix and incentives. Services and Consumables (S&C) rise from 35% of sales in 2025 to 44% by 2030. Executives receive share-based pay for the first time from 2026.
  • Pre-Approved Services (PAS), the new pay-per-use filling business. A facility costing about CHF 70m is built, and management targets about CHF 50m of PAS sales at an EBITDA margin of up to 50%. Swissmedic certification of the facility has slipped three times, partly because of SKAN's own software validation.

Evidence: the problems are in governance, management depth and the service margin.

  • The chief financial officer was convicted of insider trading at first instance on 17 November 2026, has appealed, and has been kept in office. Swiss appeals have taken two and a half to four years. The annual general meeting of 28 April 2027 is the first shareholder vote since the conviction.
  • Services leadership is doubled up on one executive since the Chief Service Officer resigned in October 2025, just as services became SKAN's priority.
  • The S&C EBITDA margin fell from 29.5% in 2024 to 20.1% in H1 2026. Nobody outside the company can split the causes between acquisition mix, PAS start-up costs and service hiring.

InferenceSKAN's behaviour changed before its narrative did. In the growth years of 2023 and 2024 SKAN hired into the growth, so it kept only 17% to 23% of each extra franc of sales as EBITDA; in H1 2026 it kept 48%. The model's 2027 margin still assumes that fixed costs grow by 8% to 10% (J2), which is cautious against five flat half-years. A cost base that has stopped growing is the internally driven lever that the estimates do not yet carry.

So what. The internal change is real but narrow. It rests on three things (conversion of the backlog, the cost base and PAS) and on a leadership team with a new chief executive, a finance chief under conviction and a gap in services leadership. The change supports margin and cash more than growth.

Against the marketThe sell-side's 2027 margin of 15.4% sits below 2024's 15.8% on 26% more sales, so the sell-side's numbers still assume SKAN's old hiring behaviour. One investor (zCapital, 30-Sep-26) says it bought SKAN for the "stronger focus on profitability", so investor thinking is a little ahead of the brokers' models. On cash the gap between the model and the FactSet figure is wider still, as the chart below shows.

Strongest counter-caseFlat costs may be the residue of a slump rather than a new discipline. No bonus was paid for 2025 and hiring was frozen, and bonuses, PAS operators, US service staff and Swiss wage inflation all return with volume. Cutting 61 people while the backlog grew 28% could itself cause the delivery slips that the case fears. And a playbook from Mettler-Toledo's short-cycle, high-volume business may not transfer to SKAN's long-cycle custom projects.

What would change my viewOn 23 March 2027, year-end headcount still near its mid-year level together with a second-half margin at or above the model's would confirm the change. Headcount back toward its end-2025 level, or a second-half S&C margin that fails to recover, would weaken it. A quantified productivity or pricing programme would strengthen it materially. A failed appeal followed by an abrupt exit of the finance chief would cost management bandwidth, although a successor with a cost-discipline mandate could later be a positive.

Conclusion: the internal change forces are moderate in breadth but improving and under-recognised; a cost base that has stopped growing is the strongest of them, and the governance overhang is the clearest drag.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. A new operator from Mettler-Toledo has held non-material costs at 104-107 for five half-years while sales swung by half (H1 2026 drop-through 48% against 17-23% in the growth years), cut headcount, introduced segment accountability, and capex is roughly halving, while PAS is a real new product line (CHF 70m plant, CHF 50m sales target) though certification has slipped three times; this is more ambition and standard than mere drift, which lifts me above the Internal group's 52. Against it sit a finance chief convicted at first instance and kept in office, a doubled-up services leadership and an S&C margin down from 29.5% to 20.1%, so the change is real but narrow and mostly repair plus margin and cash.

#3 Industry structure, competitive advantage, financial profile and management

The niche is high quality, but SKAN's economics are only average today: its advantage is shifting from the equipment it sells to the installed base it services.

Evidence: structure and advantage.

  • Position. SKAN is the largest independent isolator specialist, with an installed base of about 1,100 to 1,150 isolators and about 50 electron-beam decontamination systems. SKAN has trained nearly 700 regulators at its Allschwil site and co-writes industry containment guidance.
  • Two moats of different quality. The aftermarket moat is strong and widening: a drug process validated on a SKAN isolator needs months of revalidation to move, requalification is mandatory every year, and consumables such as closed vials (used in eight approved drugs) are written into validated processes. The new-equipment moat is strong in complex lines but narrowing in standard lines, where each line is a fresh tender.
  • Scale. Within isolators SKAN is, on the available evidence, several times the size of the next specialist. Within filling lines SKAN is small: 2025 sales of CHF 333m against Syntegon's EUR 1.75bn at a 16.1% EBITDA margin.
  • Value chain. Profit is migrating from the filling machine to validated consumables and mandatory service.

Evidence: the financial profile trails the listed peers.

  • Returns are lower than SKAN's reported figure suggests. Return on capital employed, as SKAN reports it, was 21.5% in 2024 and 10.3% in 2025. Under Swiss accounting SKAN offset CHF 86.8m of acquired goodwill against equity, so the goodwill is never amortised. Including that goodwill, the post-tax return is about 13% on a rough estimate for 2026.
  • Two accounting points cut in opposite directions against peers. Rent sits inside SKAN's EBITDA, which understates SKAN's margin by perhaps one to two points. Theoretical goodwill amortisation of about CHF 17m to 18m a year, never charged, equals about half of 2026 net profit.

Evidence: management is strong on what it controls and weak on what customers and regulators control.

  • Ambition. SKAN's targets are the most ambitious in the peer group: mid-to-upper-teens growth, an upper-teens margin, and an undated aspiration to triple sales.
  • Record. Management has delivered capacity, acquisitions and technology, but met its sales guide in only two of the last four years.
  • Ownership and controls. Two family groups hold about a third of the shares, a 10.6% holder sits on the audit committee and the former chief executive sits on the board. Controls are sound: one share class, clean audits, and no bonus paid for 2025.

InferenceSKAN's advantage is migrating from the product to the installed base, and the installed-base moat protects revenue better than it protects price: the S&C margin fell while SKAN was raising service prices. There is a link the market may miss. The service annuity is fed by equipment share with a lag of two to five years, so equipment share ceded in standard lines today is service growth forgone around 2029 to 2032.

Share ceded in standard lines today
→
Fewer SKAN isolators installed
→
Two to five years' lag
→
Service growth forgone around 2029 to 2032
So what. A high-quality niche with average but improving economics earns a premium to capital-goods companies, but not yet the multiple of the recurring-revenue peers. Two proofs would close that valuation gap: an S&C margin that stabilises, and PAS earning a return on its CHF 70m facility.

Against the marketThe share price treats SKAN as a quality compounder in recovery. I agree on the quality of the complex-line franchise and of the installed base. I differ in that turnkey erosion, the goodwill accounting and a cash conversion of a third of peers' levels are all absent from the market's narrative.

Strongest counter-caseThe margin gap to peers is the opportunity. An installed base compounding at 10% to 15% organically, a sales mix moving toward 44% services and a PAS business at an EBITDA margin of 40% or more would make SKAN resemble the recurring-revenue models of Getinge or Sartorius within five years. The bear's version is that being number one in a component whose buyers are consolidating purchases into packages is a weaker position than it looks.

What would change my viewUpward: continued wins of large US fill-finish lines and an S&C margin that recovers in the second half of 2026. Downward: a filling-machine partner defecting, or an S&C margin that keeps falling below 20%.

Conclusion: the industry structure and the installed-base moat are favourable, the financial profile is no better than average until cash conversion and the service margin prove out, and management is technically excellent but unproven on reliability.

Score: 55, set by the Rater. Qualitatively SKAN is the world number one in a regulation-gated niche with a widening installed-base moat (revalidation, annual requalification, consumables written into processes), but its new-equipment moat is narrowing in standard lines, it has no equipment pricing, is small against line builders, and management is technically excellent but unreliable on delivery with insider-leaning governance. The financial profile is ordinary (ROIC 7.2%, 54th percentile; about 13% post-tax including offset goodwill; cash conversion a third of peers; the 25th-percentile EBITDA margin is a trough year, the 91st-percentile gross margin the truer marker) and predictability is low, so it sits a touch above the four groups' average of about 49 for the quality of the niche, level with Shell and below Helios Towers.

#4 Conservatism of guidance and the record of delivery

SKAN's current guidance is realistic rather than conservative, but the new chief executive's first 2027 guide is more likely than not to set a bar that SKAN can clear.

Evidence: the 2026 guide needs a record second half.

  • The 2026 guide (set in March, confirmed in August) is "high-teens" sales growth and an EBITDA margin of 13% to 15%. Meeting that guide needs second-half sales of 222 to 232, the largest half-year in SKAN's history, at a second-half margin of 15.7% to 19.2%. The last three second halves delivered margins of 17.5%, 17.9% and 18.9%.
  • The model has second-half sales of 222.5 at an 18.4% margin, which gives growth of 16.1% and a margin of 14.5% for 2026.
  • SKAN has never raised guidance within a year, and it has issued no warning this year by late November. In 2025 it missed its sales guide after confirming the guide in August and warning on 6 November.

InferenceSKAN's guidance is realistic on sales, mildly conservative on margin and ambitious in its mid-term targets. The guiding style looks to be changing from ambitious to reliable, but no completed cycle yet proves that change. The arithmetic of the first 2027 guide is helpful: a "mid-teens" growth guide (13% to 16%) on 2026 sales of 387 implies 2027 sales of 437 to 449, with the model's 436 at the lower edge and the FactSet figure of 454 above the top. Such a guide would look conservative against the sell-side but in line with the model.

So what. Read plainly, the model's base case is a narrow miss of "high-teens" 2026 sales growth with the margin in the upper half of its range. The more valuable change would be a first 2027 guide set to be beaten, the first such guide in SKAN's listed life. That is why I put the chance of SKAN missing its 2027 guide near one in four, where SKAN's own record says one in two.

Against the marketThe sell-side sits inside the 2026 guide, above what the 2027 guide is likely to say on sales, and carries SKAN's mid-term targets forward unchanged. I put about three in ten on those mid-term targets being re-dated or lowered within 18 months, and better than even within three years.

Strongest counter-caseSKAN can meet its 2026 sales guide by a route few are watching. S&C took orders of 81.2 against sales of 64.6 in H1 2026 and its service backlog rose by half, so second-half S&C sales of 85 to 88, against 82 in the model, would close most of the gap on their own. Against that, a 2024-style slip is disclosed only with the results, so SKAN's silence does not rule one out.

What would change my viewOn 28 January 2027, 2026 sales above 392 or below 384. On 23 March 2027, the form of the 2027 guide: whether it is a range, and whether the margin range moves up a point to 14% to 16%.

Conclusion: current guidance is realistic rather than conservative and SKAN has no record of raising it, but the margin range is beatable and the new chief executive's first guide is more likely than not to set a bar that can be cleared.

Score: 38, set by the Rater. Sales guidance was met in 2022 and 2023 but missed by about four points in 2024 and by more than twenty in 2025 after being confirmed in August, guidance has never been raised within a year, the 2026 base case is a narrow miss of 'high-teens' on sales with the margin in the upper half of 13-15%, and the mid-term targets are about three in ten likely to be re-dated within 18 months. The margin record (above the top in 2023 and 2024) and a new chief executive likely to set a beatable first guide keep it off the bottom, so it sits with the Guidance group's 38, below Instalco's one-bad-year record.

#5 Pricing power, operating leverage, financial leverage, cost scope and feedback loops

Operating leverage is SKAN's only real lever: an error in the sales forecast becomes an error four to five times larger in EPS, in both directions.

Evidence.

  • Operating leverage is high and now runs in both directions. Only materials costs flex within a year, so EBITDA is roughly three-quarters of sales less a fixed block of costs (J2). The 2025 downturn and the 2026 to 2027 recovery in the boxes above show the effect.
  • SKAN's year is back-loaded. About 73% of 2026 EBITDA and about 66% of 2027 EBITDA fall in the second half.
  • Pricing power exists only in the aftermarket. Customers accept annual service and spare-part price rises because maintenance is mission-critical. Equipment, by contrast, is won in tenders, which exposes SKAN's historical price premium of up to 30% to 50%. Contracts since 2022 carry partial inflation clauses.
  • The real balance-sheet gearing is customer advances, because customers pay about 30% of a project's value on order. When orders fell 28% in 2023, operating cash flow fell to 8.7 from 61.5. When advances rose by 39 in 2025, operating cash flow reached 64.1 on lower profit.
  • Cost-out scope is limited. SKAN has no cost-reduction programme. In a downturn perhaps 10% to 15% of non-material costs could be cut, in the second year rather than the first.
  • Feedback loops. The installed-base annuity is a reinforcing loop (organic S&C growth of 10% to 15%). The turnkey loop reinforces against SKAN. Customer advances amplify the cycle in cash. PAS adoption is unproven.

InferenceRevenue growth does produce outsized profit growth at SKAN, and revenue shortfalls produce outsized profit falls. The source is operating leverage alone. What is new is that SKAN no longer hands the upside back through hiring. Equipment still decides EPS through 2029: the service annuity adds CHF 6m to 8m of EBITDA a year, while a 10% shortfall in equipment volume costs CHF 15m to 18m.

So what. Cash turns before profit in both directions, which makes customer advances the early-warning line: a downturn would show there first, as it did in 2023.

Against the marketThe sell-side's figures imply that SKAN keeps about 24% of each extra franc of sales as EBITDA in 2026 to 2028, which is the old behaviour. I expect SKAN to keep more in 2026 and 2027. I agree with the market that SKAN has no pricing power in equipment. The role of customer advances is not discussed at all.

Strongest counter-caseThe leverage that flatters the recovery would punish a slip just as hard, and with costs already held flat there is little left to cut on the way down. Larger integrated lines also carry more bought-in content: the material ratio was 29.2% in the second half of 2024 against 24.9% in the second half of 2025, a swing worth more than the whole margin upgrade.

What would change my viewA second-half 2026 margin above 19.2% would show that the leverage is larger than modelled. Year-end advances well below the mid-year level without a matching fall in backlog would be an early warning.

Conclusion: SKAN has strong operating leverage and little else, so growth does become outsized profit growth, but the same mechanism makes one delayed project a double-digit EPS event.

Score: 70, set by the Rater. Only materials (about a quarter of sales) flex within a year, so roughly 70% of costs are fixed and the leverage is proven both ways (the 2025 downturn cost 66% of lost sales at EBITDA; H1 2026 kept 48% of extra sales), with an installed-base annuity as a reinforcing loop and aftermarket prices rising 2-4% a year; forecast EPS grows about 1.6 to 2 times revenue in the outer years. It is held below 75 because there is no pricing power in equipment, financial leverage is negligible, there is no cost-out programme and the turnkey loop works against it; I sit well above the Economic strength (40) and Financial forecasts (52) groups because they grade the profile, not the gearing of the structure.

What the forecasts say

Yes

  • Double-digit growth: yes for profit, fading for revenue. Revenue grows at double digits to 2028 and at about 9% after. EBITDA compounds at about 15.5% a year from 2026 to 2030, and model EPS at about 18%.
  • Higher margins than in the past: yes. The EBITDA margin passes its 2024 peak in 2027 and reaches 17% by 2029, against a range of 13.7% to 15.8% in 2021 to 2024.
  • The largest change against history is cash. Free cash flow was a cumulative (40) in 2021 to 2025 on FactSet's definition; the model has about +161 in 2026 to 2030. The balance sheet moves from modest net debt to roughly net cash by 2028 to 2030. The model's own net debt line reads CHF 15m to 25m too high, mainly because of how the model times dividends and treats the reported first half.

No, or not yet

  • Higher growth than in the past: no. Revenue compounds at 11.6% a year from the depressed 2025 base and at only about 8% from the 2024 peak, against about 17% a year in 2020 to 2024.
  • Recovery first, progress second. Model EPS regains its 2024 level only in 2027, on about 21% more revenue. Progress beyond the old peak starts in 2028.

InferenceThe 2027 forecast is demonstrably achievable because of where its profit comes from. Of the CHF 31m increase in EBITDA between 2025 and 2027, about 21 is the equipment segment returning to what it earned in 2024 on the same sales, and about 10 is S&C growing at a margin below each of its last three full years. PAS contributes nothing, and no price increase is needed. From 2027 to 2030 the character of the growth changes: about 40% of the EBITDA increase comes from PAS, a regulated service that SKAN has never run and for which no customer has been disclosed.

So what. Put high weight on the 2026 forecast, moderate weight on 2027 and low weight on 2028 onward. The model leans later than the sell-side on the timing of sales, while matching the sell-side on profit for the next two years.

Against the marketFor 2026 and 2027 the model's EBITDA is level with the FactSet figure (+0.4% and (0.4)%) on 2% and 4% less sales. For 2028 and 2029 the model's EBITDA is 8% and 18% lower, and its attributable EPS is 15% and 24% lower. Part of that gap is with one unnamed broker who alone supplies the 2029 figure and grows sales at 17% to 20%; against UBS, the model's 2028 sales are 4.7% lower.

Strongest counter-caseThe forecasts may be too cautious twice over: on the 2027 margin (J2) and on the 2028 order rate (J3). Together those two would put 2028 model EPS at about 2.5 to 2.7, above the FactSet figure. The opposite case is a 2025-type year in 2027, with attributable EPS near 0.96.

What would change my viewThe thresholds in topic #9. A dated PAS certification with a named customer would raise my weight on 2028 to 2030.

Conclusion: the forecasts show double-digit profit growth and record margins but slower revenue growth than in the past, with 2027 a well-founded recovery to old earnings and the years beyond dependent on PAS and an order rate that are not yet proven.

Score: 90, set by the Rater. Growth of 15-30% gives A, honest in that it is organic and the margin path rises from 14.5% to 17.3%, above the 13.7-15.8% of 2021-24. I place it at the floor because the first years are a recovery (EPS regains its 2024 level only in 2027 on 21% more revenue), revenue grows more slowly than in the past, and about 40% of the 2027-30 EBITDA gain rests on unproven PAS.

#7 Scope for upgrades to guidance, estimates and the narrative over 6 to 12 months

The upgrade engine is the margin, not sales, and its first clear test is the August 2027 half-year report.

Evidence: the expected path of revisions, event by event.

28 January 2027, preliminary figures. 2026 sales of about 385 to 392, against the FactSet figure of 396, imply a trim of 1% to 3% to sales estimates, carried into later years through the lower base. Order intake matters more: above about 220 it holds or raises 2027 and 2028 estimates; below about 180 it cuts them by 3% to 5%.
23 March 2027, results and the first 2027 guide. I expect a small beat on the 2026 margin on lower sales. For 2027 I expect the sell-side's sales to move from 454 toward 440 to 445 and its margin from 15.4% toward 15.6% to 16.0%, leaving EPS between (4)% and +1%. Free cash flow estimates should rise.
August 2027, half-year report. The first event at which an upgrade to the current year is more likely than a cut: 40% raised, 35% unchanged, 25% cut. By then a flat cost base would have shown in three consecutive half-years, against an easy first-half comparison.
From January 2028. The 2028 and 2029 estimates meet the 2027 order intake and the 2028 guide.

InferenceSKAN can beat 2027 EPS estimates without beating sales estimates. On the model's lower 2027 sales, an EBITDA margin of 17.5% gives attributable EPS of about 1.98, 7% above the FactSet figure; a margin of 18% gives about 2.06, 12% above (my arithmetic, holding depreciation, financial items and tax as modelled). The bull case in topic #9 pairs that margin with on-schedule sales.

So what. The scope for upgrades over 6 to 12 months is modest, specific and back-ended to August 2027, and SKAN cannot raise guidance before then. The narrative has more room than the numbers: it can move from "orders recovered" to "delivery proven, on a leaner SKAN that now generates cash", and the share price does not yet contain that second chapter.

Against the marketEvery visible broker rating is Buy and the mean target is at the share price, so the sell-side has nothing left to argue without raising its estimates or its multiple. I think the brokers will raise margins, trim sales and leave EPS about where it is. One cosmetic risk: UBS's 2026 EPS of 1.54 implies that tax and minorities take only about 14% of pre-tax profit, against about 20% on the model's inputs, so UBS's EPS may be cut even if its EBITDA is right.

Strongest counter-caseUpgrades could come sooner and broader. Strong second-half orders would lift the model's own 2028 forecast toward UBS's, a second-half margin above the guided range would pull 2027 margin estimates up in March rather than August, and a certification with a named PAS customer would add a third source of upgrades. The opposite case is a year-end slip, after which SKAN's thin broker coverage would turn one broker's cut into the whole revision.

What would change my viewA quantified productivity or pricing programme in March would bring the upgrade forward. A 2027 guide that brackets the sell-side's sales would remove the trim to sales estimates that I expect.

Conclusion: there is real but limited scope for upgrades, concentrated in margin and cash and most likely from August 2027, while the outer-year estimates are more likely to fall than rise.

Score: 42, set by the Rater. Guidance, which counts most, cannot be raised before August 2027, when the memo puts a raise at 40% against a 25% cut, and the first 2027 guide is more likely to sit below the sell-side on sales (55%); consensus 2027 EPS is more likely cut than raised (40% against 25%) and 2028 clearly so (55% against 15%), with a margin and cash upgrade engine that leaves near-term EPS about flat against 13% revenue growth, so the size ratio is near nil to slightly negative. The narrative has more room (to 'delivery proven, leaner, cash-generating'), which lifts it above the fourth-set group's 34, between Tele2 and IMCD.

#8 Current momentum: guidance, estimates, narrative, price, and peers

Evidence: estimates and targets.

  • Sell-side estimates have gone nowhere for six months. The 2027 EPS figure moved 0%, 0%, +4% and (30)% over one, three, six and twelve months, and 2027 EBITDA was trimmed 4% in the last month.
  • Sell-side targets have risen without estimates. Target prices rose 9% in three months and 15% in six with estimates flat, to a mean of CHF 72; UBS has CHF 77.

Evidence: the share price.

  • The share price is strong but slowing. The price stands 23% above its 200-day average, but its climb has slowed: +41% over six months and +6% over three.
  • The rally was mostly a re-rating. From CHF 42.1 at 20.8x in March 2026 to CHF 75.0 at 32.0x in October, the price rose 78%: 54% from the multiple and 16% from forward EPS, and most of the 16% is the passage of time rolling the earnings window forward (my arithmetic from the monthly history).

Evidence: narrative, peers and positioning.

  • Narrative. The market's story is "orders have recovered". The conviction of the finance chief has drawn no estimate, rating or proxy-adviser response yet.
  • Peers: the rebound has been multiple-led across the group. Among SKAN's twelve sector peers on the dashboard, only Tecan and Oxford Instruments carry an A for earnings momentum, and most carry C or worse even though most of their share prices rose. Tecan is up 88% in twelve months and Sartorius 27%. Repligen has beaten and raised its guidance three times this year. Stevanato fell 28% on 3 November on its GLP-1 reset.
  • Co-movement and positioning. Peers explain only 16% of SKAN's daily share-price moves, but a third to a half of SKAN's six-month re-rating looks like a sector-wide tide. Deutsche Bank (20-Nov-26) has European small caps at a deep underweight and healthcare at an overweight; Morgan Stanley expects the rotation into defensive stocks to unwind.

InferenceSKAN's momentum is strong in price and absent in earnings. The slowing of the share price over the last three months, as the multiple reached its long-run median, is what a re-rating looks like when it has done its work and is waiting for earnings.

So what. On the test of strong momentum in guidance and sell-side upgrades, SKAN does not pass today; on price and theme it does. The next move in the share price needs estimates to start rising, or it will rely on the sector tide.

Against the marketA reader of the share-price chart and of an all-Buy sell-side would call SKAN's momentum strong. I call it split, and the weaker half, earnings, is the half that sustains a rally.

Strongest counter-caseMultiples lead earnings at turning points. In the precedent set, the rallies at Lonza, Repligen, Ypsomed, GEA and Stratec all began as multiple expansion and were validated when estimates followed. A record backlog covering 1.2x sales is one of the markers that those sustained cases shared.

What would change my viewThe first positive revisions to a current-year EPS estimate would tip momentum to strong. Estimate cuts while the share price holds would be a warning.

Conclusion: price and thematic momentum are strong, sell-side earnings momentum is weak and guidance momentum is nil, so momentum is one-legged until estimates turn.

Score: 75, set by the Rater. Both measures positive with none strongly negative gives B; the price is 23% above its 200-day average, targets are up 15% in six months and every rating is Buy. I place it at the floor of the band because the parts behind the sell-side reading are weak (the memo has 2027 EPS flat over one and three months, EBITDA trimmed 4% in the last month and a D on earnings momentum, against figures.md's older +12%), guidance is held not raised, price momentum has slowed to +6% over three months, and the peer rebound is multiple-led.

#9 Riskiness and simplicity of the forecasts and expectations

The SKAN case is simple to state and hard to time: the business is not fragile, but the calendar of customer deliveries is.

Simplicity: one driver, one opaque link. For the next 18 months the case has close to one driver: the dates on which a few dozen equipment projects reach manufacturing and assembly, the stage at which 75% to 80% of their value is recognised as sales. From sales down to EPS the chain is clean, with no adjusted-profit layer, low debt and a flat share count. The one opaque link is the conversion of backlog into sales, and customers control it.

What the forecasts require, in order

1. Customers take delivery on schedule (achieved in two of the last four years).
→
2. The cost base holds while record volume is delivered (shown for one half-year with rising sales).
→
3. The S&C margin stops falling at about 22% to 23% (not yet shown).
→
4. From 2028, PAS ramps up and the order rate holds (neither yet shown).

The range of outcomes for 2027 attributable EPS

The 2027 range runs 45% below the base case and 21% above it. The downward skew does not come from the margin, which, with a flat cost base, responds equally in both directions. It comes from the distribution of sales itself: deliveries can slip but cannot be pulled forward. For 2026 the range is narrow, with attributable EPS of 1.20 to 1.57.

Suddenness and trackability: news arrives in steps, but every driver is disclosed. SKAN reports twice a year, shows the decisive second half only once, three months after it ends, and gives no phasing of its backlog. What SKAN does disclose is useful: orders, backlog, segment EBITDA, headcount and customer advances together reveal every driver. The next readings, with their thresholds, are below.

By 31 December 2026: PAS certification, SKAN's stated aim. The model assumes certification in H1 2027, so a slip is already in the numbers and a certification would be a free positive.

I expect the January and March 2027 readings together to remove about a third of the 2027 range of outcomes.

InferencePredictability is low for an 18-month forecast and reasonable for a three-year one, because over three years delivery timing largely nets out.

So what. Hold the forecasts as an earnings level with a range of dates, and expect the share price to move in jumps on two or three days a year.

Sudden risks, by expected damage.

A large project postponed or cancelled (one item is at risk, and a CHF 40m GLP-1 project has no disclosed restart date); a failed appeal by the finance chief; Swissmedic refusing or long delaying PAS certification; a quality or site-integration failure on a complex line; a filling-machine partner switching to its own isolators; a franc shock.

Risks to the share price beyond fundamentals.

SKAN is small (a market value of about CHF 1.56bn), trades USD 3m to 5m a day and is covered by two or three broker models that are all at Buy, so one broker changing its mind is the consensus changing its mind.

How far the shares could fall. Three downside markers bracket the risk.

CHF 55 to 57de-rating to the 10th-percentile multiple with estimates intact (about (20)%)
CHF 40 to 45a moderate miss ((36)% to (43)%)
CHF 35.652-week low, set after the 2025 warning: the severe case

Sector precedent: SKAN's rally is now in its reality-check window. In a study of 14 life-science and pharmaceutical-equipment companies, rallies led by the multiple met a reality check 6 to 12 months after they began, at one of the next two to four reports. The rallies were sustained where estimates then rose, and reversed where a miss or a cut came, as at Tecan in 2024, Chemometec in March 2026 and Stevanato this month. SKAN's rally began in spring 2026, so its window runs from now to next spring. Customer concentration and thin broker coverage marked the reversals, and SKAN has both; high backlog cover marked the survivors, and SKAN has that too.

Strongest counter-case: the risk is overstated.SKAN's risks are named, dated and mostly deferral rather than loss. The items that hurt in 2025 (vaccine lines, one GLP-1 project and the at-risk item) are identified and outside the plan, and no warning has come this year. S&C now supplies about 57% of EBITDA, so even if equipment repeated 2025 the group would earn EBITDA of about 49. Over three years, timing risk largely nets out. What does not net out is the order rate after 2027, share loss in standard lines and PAS.

Against the marketThe market's narrative acknowledges postponements in words but not in numbers: the FactSet 2027 EPS figure sits between my base and bull cases. I weight a mild miss or worse at about one in three.

What would change my viewA disclosed phasing of the backlog, or quarterly order reporting, would cut the riskiness more than any single result.

Conclusion: the case is simple to state and hard to time, with a wide range of 2027 outcomes that is skewed down by customer-controlled delivery dates, a share price that adjusts in steps, and risks that are mostly identifiable and mostly about the path.

Score: 28, set by the Rater. The case is simple and low-debt, but for 18 months it rests on one customer-controlled driver, the timing of a few dozen projects, which operating leverage turns into a 2027 EPS cone of 45% below to 21% above the base (2.3% of sales is 14% of EPS), news arrives in half-yearly steps with no backlog phasing, and the stock is small, illiquid and covered by two or three all-Buy models in a sector where multiple-led rallies met a reality check within 6-12 months. Risks are mostly deferral not loss and S&C now gives about 57% of EBITDA, which keeps it off the bottom; between the two Risks groups (28 and 38) and below Helios Towers.

#10 Where the stock is in its lifecycle

SKAN's fundamentals are turning up, matching the dashboard's starting phase of Turning/Inflecting, but its share price behaves as if the thesis were already broadening.

Evidence, by the three tests.

  • Momentum (#8) gives two readings. The share price behaves like a thesis that is broadening. Estimates behave like those of a stock that has only just turned: they stopped falling six months ago and have not started to rise.
  • Scope for upgrades (#7) is real but modest, and mostly from August 2027.
  • Risk (#9) is still that of an early recovery: SKAN has passed one delivery test (H1 2026), and the decisive one (H2 2026) is unreported.

InferenceThe gap between the share price and the fundamentals closes in one of two ways: estimates rise and the phase becomes thesis broadening, or the share price waits for them. Stalling is the third path, and it would look like 2028 estimates being cut while the multiple sits at its median.

So what. A stock that is turning up deserves a multiple below the one it would earn in full delivery, because its forecasts are still uncertain. That point bears directly on the fair multiple in topic #11.

What moves SKAN forward a phase.

A delivered second half of 2026, a flat cost base confirmed, the first upgrade to a current-year estimate and a PAS certification would make SKAN a thesis-broadening stock by autumn 2027.

What moves SKAN back a phase.

A year-end delivery slip, weak second-half orders, or a 2028 guide that steps down to low-teens growth with nothing new to replace the old growth story.

Against the marketAn all-Buy sell-side with targets at the share price implies a view that the recovery is established. I think the recovery is one good half-year old.

Strongest counter-caseThe phase may already be broadening: new holders are arriving for the profitability story, and the first evidence of the flat cost base predates the March results.

Conclusion: SKAN is turning up, with a share price that already behaves as if the thesis were broadening and fundamentals that have one more delivery test to pass before it is.

Score: 60, set by the Rater. The memo's Turning up, matching the computed Turning/Inflecting, is right for the fundamentals: estimates stopped falling six months ago but have not risen, and the decisive second-half delivery is unreported. But the price is a phase ahead (54 of its 78% rally was multiple, now at its ten-year median), so the attractive early-turn point is partly spent and the next six months are the sector's reality-check window; it sits below Reply's turning with positive revisions and just under Nexans.

#11 The fair multiple

The guideline fair multiple of 34.8x is the right destination but a generous starting point: on the model's earnings, SKAN already trades close to it.

The guideline. 34.8x two-year-forward earnings, the 60th percentile of SKAN's own history, as set for a stock in the Turning/Inflecting phase.

Evidence.

  • SKAN's valuation history is short and uneven. SKAN has 59 months of data. It traded at 64x in December 2021, just after listing, mostly between 35x and 45x from mid-2022 to August 2024, and at 18.7x at the trough in October 2025. It has not traded above 32.0x at any month-end since August 2024. The ten-year bands are 23.9x (tenth percentile), 32.7x (median), 38.5x (75th) and 44.7x (90th); the median of the last two years is 25.6x.
  • Today's multiple depends on whose earnings are used. It is 28.6x on the sell-side's EPS, 31.7x on model EPS and about 33x to 35x on attributable EPS, so the discount to the guideline is 22%, 10% or roughly 0% to 5%.
  • Even the bullish brokers are not using 34.8x. The mean target of CHF 72 and UBS's CHF 77 are about 30x and 32.5x the EPS that the sell-side has two years out today.

Why 34.8x is defensible.

SKAN has traded above 34.8x in a little under half of its listed months, each time when the market believed in mid-teens growth with a rising margin. The model has EPS growing 14% to 26% a year through 2030, cash flow inflecting and the balance sheet moving to net cash. Sartorius trades on 39x current earnings.

Why 34.8x is generous for now.

  1. The high multiples of 2021 to 2024 were paid on estimates that were later cut by a third to a half. They record what optimists paid before two misses, not what the business proved to be worth.
  2. At end-2027 the multiple is applied to 2029 earnings, the year in which the model is furthest below the sell-side and which leans most on PAS. A full multiple on the least proven year is a demanding pairing.
  3. The quality markers are mixed (#3): cash conversion of 0.3x to 0.4x until 2028, a return on capital of about 13% including goodwill, a governance overhang of uncertain length, and earnings that carry no goodwill amortisation.

Where I come out: the fair multiple depends on which path the next two results confirm.

34.8xbase-to-bull path: March and August 2027 confirm the leaner cost base and orders hold
Low 30splain base path, with outer-year estimates drifting down toward the model's: near the ten-year median
24x to 26xif a year of sales slips

Against the marketThe standard statement is that SKAN trades "below its historical median". That statement is true on the sell-side's EPS and untrue on the model's. Nobody has yet said so.

Strongest counter-caseThe guideline may be too low. If SKAN delivers and the cost discipline holds, it would be a regulated-niche leader with mid-teens EPS growth, a rising recurring share of sales and its first decade of free cash flow, and such companies have held 38x or more for years. The opposite case is that a lumpy equipment maker with two misses in three years belongs at its two-year median of 25.6x.

What would change my viewEstimates rising after March, or the governance overhang clearing, would make 34.8x my central case. Cuts to 2028 estimates together with a 2028 guide stepping down would make the median multiple the ceiling.

Conclusion: the guideline fair multiple of 34.8x is achievable if the next two results confirm the leaner SKAN, but on the plain base case I expect the low 30s, and on the model's earnings the share is already close to its guideline.

Score: 54, set by the Rater. Neutral on the only readable measure gives C. I place it just above mid-band but not high: the 38th percentile rests on the sell-side's EPS (28.6x), while on model or attributable EPS the stock is at 31.7-35x, at or above the 32.7x median, and a turning-up stock with a history built on estimates later cut by a third to a half deserves no more than its median today.

#12 Total shareholder return

The three-year return is robust because it is earnings; the 18-month return depends on a re-rating, and its probability-weighted value is close to today's price.

What drives each part of the return

  • Earnings: growth already in the forecasts, not an upgrade. The return capitalises two-year-forward EPS, which rolls from about 2.17 today to about 2.41 at end-2027, in effect moving onto 2028 to 2029 earnings as time passes.   • The multiple: one step, taken once. A single re-rating from 31.7x on model EPS to 34.8x, taken once and then held.
  • Dividends and other cash returns: small today, with optionality later. A 30% payout gives a yield under 1%, and there are no buybacks. The balance sheet reaches roughly net cash around 2028, which creates capacity for cash returns or bolt-on acquisitions from 2029 that is not in the numbers.

With no re-rating the three-year return is still about +34% (roughly 12% a year), and if the multiple fell to its tenth percentile, earnings growth of 32% would leave the holder about flat.

18 months: about 40% of the return is the re-rating.
Three years: about +34% with no re-rating; about flat even at the tenth-percentile multiple.

A rough cross-check on the next 13 months (mine, approximate): the most likely outcome is a gain of about a fifth, but the expected outcome is small. Setting the four 2027 scenarios of topic #9 against plausible share prices gives about CHF 33 in the bear case, about CHF 50 in a mild miss where revenue is deferred and the multiple retreats, about CHF 83 in the base case and about CHF 95 in the bull case. The probability-weighted value is about CHF 70 to 72, close to today's price, because the one-in-three tail is deep. The January and March 2027 readings are what will move those probabilities.

Against the marketBrokers' targets imply about 3% to 10% upside. The model's value is above those targets because it applies a higher multiple to lower earnings.

Strongest counter-caseIf the margin and order judgements (J2 and J3) both resolve favourably, two-year-forward EPS at end-2027 is nearer 2.7 than 2.4, and the return at an unchanged multiple is as large as the model's return with the re-rating. The opposite case is the downside arithmetic of topic #9.

What would change my viewThe readings listed in topic #9; after 23 March 2027 the scenario weights can be reset with real information.

Conclusion: the model's return of +23.5% to end-2027 and +47.3% to mid-2029 is driven mainly by earnings growth already in the forecasts plus a one-off re-rating, and the three-year return is far more robust than the 18-month one because it does not need the re-rating.

Score: 32, set by the Rater. About +2% sits in D and maps to about 30; I lift it slightly because the three-year check is strong (+47% at the guideline, about +34% with no re-rating, mostly earnings) and the modal outcome is about +20%, but hold it low in the band because the one-in-three lower tail is deep (CHF 33-50) and the 18-month return leans on a re-rating.

#13 Summary conclusion

The strong part: quality, volume and a cost base that has stopped growing

SKAN is a high-quality niche franchise at an early and well-evidenced point in its recovery. Regulation and a record order book give SKAN volume. A new operator has stopped the cost base growing, and the heavy investment years are over. The earnings that result through 2027 are earnings the business has made before. This strong part of the case is stronger on margin and cash than the market's numbers yet show.

The weak part: price, outer-year estimates and timing

The share price has already rebuilt its multiple on falling estimates, the outer-year estimates look too high, and the timing of profit is in customers' hands. Near-term changes to estimates should therefore be benign and small, and the probability-weighted 13-month value is close to today's price.
The route to the kind of situation Richard looks for, with outcomes and upgrades unusually skewed to the positive, is evidence that the leaner cost base survives a record half of deliveries and that orders are holding. Both are testable on two dates, 28 January and 23 March 2027. If both tests pass, the margin arithmetic of J2 points to 2027 EPS 7% to 12% above the sell-side's even on the model's lower sales, and the stock moves from turning up to thesis broadening with a fair multiple to match. Over three years the case is more forgiving, because the return is earnings and the main risk is the path.

The four memo ratings

Thesis's Change Forces' Strength: 70, set by the Rater. Strong, enacted external demand (70) already in a record backlog and a narrower but real internal shift to cost discipline and lower capex (60) reach profits as model EPS compounding about 18% with margins above any past year (A at the floor), because the 2027 step-up is earnings the business has made before. It is held below 75 because the forces deliver volume without price, the first two years are recovery rather than progress, and the post-2027 profit growth leans on unproven PAS and an order rate that may plateau.

Foundations' Robustness: 52, set by the Rater. A regulation-protected niche leadership with a widening installed-base moat and low debt (Quality 55) is offset by ordinary economics (weak cash conversion, a falling service margin, eroding share in standard lines), low predictability and a delivery record of two sales misses in three years with no in-year raise (Guidance 38). It sits below Judges Scientific's 60 because, unlike that case, the cash conversion is poor and the governance overhang adds to the misses.

Setups' Fit/Crispness: 66, set by the Rater. The case fits 'CfC in quality cyclical at trough-on-trough, leading to reversion to normal' in substance: a 2025 trough, the cause for concern (orders and costs) clearing with record backlog and five flat cost half-years, and a reversion to earnings already earned in 2024. I score above the memo's C because the multiple having already recovered is price, not fit; it is held in the 60s because the quality is middling and today's problems (falling S&C margin, a convicted finance chief kept in office, the unproven second-half delivery) blur the mechanism, like Richard's CVS Group case.

Case Riskiness: 27, set by the Rater. A simple, low-debt case does not offset a wide, down-skewed 2027 cone ((45)%/+21%) driven by one customer-controlled timing variable that operating leverage magnifies, stepwise half-yearly disclosure, and a small illiquid stock on a few all-Buy models whose multiple-led rally is in its reality-check window (Riskiness 28). Deferral rather than loss and a growing service floor keep it above Judges Scientific's 20.

End notes: how to read the numbers

  • Price. CHF 70.1 (23-Nov-26). The Financial Analyst's model strikes its return from CHF 68.80 (19-Nov-26).
  • Forecasts. The forecasts are the model's (update 2). I have changed no forecast input: my analysis moves the skew around the base case, not the base case itself, and I have no evidence that the earlier work did not already weigh.
  • Two EPS bases. "Model EPS" is before minority interests, because the model does not deduct them. Brokers publish EPS after minorities ("attributable EPS"), which on the model's forecasts is 0.05 to 0.08 lower. I name the basis each time.
  • "The FactSet figure" is FactSet's median. It rests on two or three brokers, of which only UBS is named, so I do not call it consensus. "Viewforth" in chart labels means the model's forecasts.
  • The market's view is inferred. No broker note on SKAN itself could be retrieved. I read the market from the brokers' numbers, targets and ratings, the share price, analysts' questions on calls and one fund letter.
  • Abbreviations. E&S is Equipment and Solutions (isolators and filling-line systems, about 62% of 2026 sales). S&C is Services and Consumables (the aftermarket of the installed base, about 38%). PAS is Pre-Approved Services, the new pay-per-use filling business, reported inside S&C. ADC is antibody-drug conjugate. GLP-1 refers to the class of weight-loss and diabetes drugs. Capex is capital spending; ROIC is return on invested capital; CfC is cause for concern.
  • Charts drawn for this page (visuals/drawn/ and visuals/drawn-copy-editor/) take their figures from the memo. Default visuals are from FactSet, the Master Dashboard and the Financial Analyst's model, as noted under each.
